text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Scandinavian Airline System, SAS, has been criticised by enviromental organisation Naturvernforbundet for calling the company's new planes enviromentally friendly. Anne Johanne Enger in Naturnvernforbundet says the enviromental benefit from new planes will be counterbalanced by increased growth in air traffic. Niels Erik Nertun of SAS, says the airliner's image is worse than the company's own environmental studies indicate.

- Telecommunications company Nera has developed a satellite telephone which can make calls, send faxs, data and e-mail from almost anywere on earth. Norwegian Telenor Satellite Services is working with Britain's British Telecom to offer a global services with the new system.

- Norway's largest privately-owned oil company, Saga Petroleum ASA, is considering making a bid to take over British company Santa Fe Exploration, which is valued at almost $1 billion. Saga will make an offer by November 1.
- Due to new effective drugs for depression and migrain, sales of pharmaceuticals rose by 13.3 percent betwwen 1994 to 1995. Total sales in 1995 reached 7.6 billion crowns.
- Shipping company Smedvig is refinancing its loan portfolio. Ole Melberg, head of Smedvig, says he is satisfied with the new agreements, but will not comment on how much Smedvig's savings are.
